Topic 1.4: Effective LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Effective LISTENING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we LISTENING communication learner should be able to: Simon says, in small groups communicate?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag
2. listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EFFECTIVE LISTENING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Effective LISTENING helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: EFFECTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag

What this means
In this part you learn to listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Effective LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements

What this means
In this part you learn to listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Effective LISTENING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Effective LISTENING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Effective LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Effective LISTENING to a partner. (skill: listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Effective LISTENING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag.
3. Practise this skill: listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Effective LISTENING from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Effective LISTENING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Effective LISTENING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we LISTENING communication learner should be able to: Simon says, in small groups communicate?
2. How do we b) listen and communicate effectively  Learners are provided with communicate?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Effective LISTENING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: listen with increased attention to  Learners engage in story telling indigenous 2 lessons rhymes, songs, conversations and  Learners listen to audio or audiovisual languag.
5. Be able to: listen to experiences of others and  Learners listen and pick out respond appropriately to the vocabulary from material listened to feelings and ideas expressed  Learners listen to daily announcements.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
